title: Hotfix: cap tier label cardinality in runtime metrics
author: Logan Wright
description:
Context: During early canary for tiered batching defaults, we saw a sudden increase in metrics time-series count and ingestion cost. Root cause was effectively-unbounded cardinality for the `batching_tier` label in several runtime metrics: in override/migration paths we were emitting user-provided strings (e.g., legacy profile names / policy-derived values) rather than a strict enum, causing a new label value per tenant/route. This PR hotfixes the runtime to strictly bound tier label cardinality to a small allowlist and moves detailed identifiers to tracing where cardinality is safe.

What changed: 1) Canonicalize `batching_tier` to enum values only: {fast, standard, cost_efficient, unset}. Any unrecognized value maps to `unset` and increments a counter for visibility. 2) Remove `effective_profile_id` (string) from metric labels; it is now emitted as a span attribute on `scheduler.profile_selection` only. 3) Add a hard guard in the metrics wrapper: if `batching_tier` label value is not one of the enum strings, we replace it before export. 4) Add tests that assert max tier label cardinality <= 4 for the affected metrics. 5) Update internal docs in-code comments to prevent future re-introductions.

Affected metrics (examples): `runtime.scheduler.queue_latency_ms{batching_tier=...}`, `runtime.scheduler.batch_size_tokens{batching_tier=...}`, `runtime.decode.token_latency_ms{batching_tier=...}`.

Why this is safe: This only changes metric label values and where we attach detailed identifiers (metrics -> tracing). No scheduling behavior changes. Dashboards expecting tier breakdown continue to work; they will see `unset` rather than a long tail of custom strings.

Rollout: Land on main ASAP, then backport to the runtime-1.22 release branch prior to expanding canary. SRE will monitor (a) active series count, (b) metrics ingestion rate, and (c) `runtime.metrics.tier_label_sanitized_total` after deploy.

Follow-ups (not in this hotfix): audit other high-cardinality labels (route_id, policy_id) and apply the same guardrail pattern; add a CI lint that rejects non-enum label assignment for tier/reason-code dimensions.
commits: metrics: canonicalize batching_tier label values to enum
tracing: attach effective_profile_id as span attr (remove from metrics)
metrics: add sanitizer + counter for invalid tier label values
tests: assert tier label cardinality stays bounded

conversation:
Allison Grant (review): We should be explicit about the allowed values. Also can we guarantee we never export arbitrary strings again? Author (Logan Wright): Added `TierLabel::to_str()` mapping + sanitizer in the metrics wrapper; all call sites now go through the enum. Also added a unit test that fails if we emit >4 values.

Caleb Johnson (review): Moving `effective_profile_id` out of metrics is the right call. Please ensure the span attr is on the same trace as the scheduler decision span so we can still debug. Author: Updated `scheduler.profile_selection` span to include `effective_profile_id` and `selection_source` attributes; verified in local trace capture.

Aisha Bello (SRE): Can we get a counter so we can detect if something is still attempting to emit custom tiers? Author: Added `runtime.metrics.tier_label_sanitized_total{metric=...}` and logged at debug once per minute (rate-limited) when non-enum values are observed.

Julian Moore (runtime): One concern: mapping unknown -> unset might hide misconfig. Author: Agreed; we increment the counter and include `selection_source` in the span, so we still see why. Also added a warning in code comments and the internal guideline doc.

Allison Grant: Approved after test added + docs comment. Caleb Johnson: Approved. Aisha Bello: Approved (requesting backport ASAP).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Logan Wright. Hotfix requested by SRE after canary metrics series spike; coordinated with runtime-1.22 release train.
release_notes: Runtime telemetry: bounded `batching_tier` metric label cardinality (fast/standard/cost_efficient/unset). Detailed profile identifiers now emitted via tracing instead of metrics labels.
backport_notes: Backport required to release/runtime-1.22 before further canary expansion. Cherry-pick target: `release/runtime-1.22` (no conflicts expected). If conflicts arise, prioritize: (1) sanitizer in metrics wrapper, (2) removal of `effective_profile_id` label, (3) unit test. Notify #eng-sre and #eng-releases after backport lands so dashboards/alerts can be re-validated.
